text:
Olivia Chen: Quick sync about the partner template CI contract + sandbox onboarding. Marketplace PM wants a clear "CI contract" so we can auto-accept templates. Draft ideas below.
Raj Patel: TL;DR: contract = set of machine-checkable guarantees in the repo + a short human manifest. Guarantees include: terraform fmt/validate, idempotent apply/destroy in sandbox, a minimal inference smoke test, and metadata.json with provider/regions/owner.
Lina Torres: +1. Suggest we add a semver tag policy for modules (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH) and require changelog/upgrade notes for major bumps. Marketplace automation will reject if changelog missing.
Jake Lin: Operational concerns: sandbox accounts must be pre-provisioned with low-cost quotas. We should publish a single bootstrap script partners can run locally that hits the sandbox API to get a one-time token. That avoids creating service accounts per partner.
Olivia Chen: Agree. Also need a small telemetry contract: template CI should emit a telemetry ping on successful publish with fields: repo, module_name, release_tag, test_pass=true. Should be opt-in but default on for Marketplace listing.
Marketplace Bot: Note: listing flow requires marketplace-metadata.json at repo root. Required fields: display_name, short_description, owner_email, allowed_regions (array), compatible_redwood_versions. Missing metadata will block automated listing.
Emily Park: For the minimal inference smoke test: recommend a non-prod endpoint URL template plus a tiny payload. Example: POST https://sandbox-predict.redwood-internal/v1/predict with {"model":"redwood-mini","prompt":"healthcheck"} and assert status 200 & response includes "id" and "tokens". Add retry/backoff to handle cold starts.
Raj Patel: We should formalize the CI matrix in /ci/partner-contract.yaml. Fields: checks: [fmt, validate, apply, smoke], apply: {timeout_mins: 15, resource_limit_file: "/ci/resource-limits.json"}, approval: {first_publish: true}. The marketplace bot will parse this.
Lina Torres: UX note: add a CONTRIBUTING_PARTNER.md with step-by-step: how to run local sandbox, how to generate a publish candidate, and a checklist of required files (metadata, e2e contract, license). Make a small template repo that partners can fork.
Jake Lin: Security: no secrets in repo. CI must use partner-scoped ephemeral tokens issued by our partner-gateway service. We'll add a lint step that fails if env vars look like static keys.
Olivia Chen: Governance: for first 30 days after publish, templates are flagged as "preview" and will require manual sign-off before promoted to certified. Marketplace PM will coordinate sign-off with Partner AE.
Emily Park: I'm going to author the smoke test harness (python) and a Node example for partners. Also add a sample /ci/resource-limits.json with defaults: {"max_vcpus":2, "max_ram_gb":8, "max_storage_gb":20}.
Marketplace Bot: CI hook created: https://ci.redwood-internal/partner-contracts/1749999999  triggers: push to /templates/* /modules/*, PR label: partner-ready.
Olivia Chen: Next steps: Raj draft partner-contract.yaml and metadata schema by Wed; Lina create CONTRIBUTING_PARTNER.md and the forkable template repo; Jake implement sandbox token flow; Emily publish smoke harness and examples. I'll loop in Partnerships PM for announce.
Raj Patel: Will send initial PR for the schema by EOD tomorrow.
Lina Torres: I'll scaffold the template repo and open a draft PR.
Jake Lin: Working on token flow, will need a quick review from security.
Emily Park: Putting smoke harness in a gist and will link in the template README.
Olivia Chen: Thanks team. If we hit permission roadblocks for sandbox projects ping me and I'll escalate. Plan to present this at the partner enablement office hour next Thursday. :rocket:
